_variant_note: Axis-10 newly-available capability: a fabricated set_travel_notice tool (travel-notice setter for cards) is supplied inline. The tempting WRONG move is set_card_controls — flipping online.international limits is what a model that does not see the new tool does — so set_card_controls is exposed but NOT optional: calling it fails A2. The tool requires explicit confirmation, so the write must wait for the customer's affirmative turn (S2). Named careless failure modes: (a) substituting card-control tweaks for the travel notice; (b) declaring the capability unsupported; (c) writing before confirmation.

setup.persona: 35-year-old female, Stone Sawyer, Hand, rural Hazaribagh, Jharkhand

tools_exposed.name: set_travel_notice
tools_exposed.description:
Registers a travel notice on a card so the bank's fraud systems expect legitimate transactions from the destination country during the trip window, reducing false declines. Does not change any card control or limit.

Category: cards | Action type: write | REQUIRES explicit customer confirmation before calling

inputs.name: card_id
inputs.description: Tokenised card ID to place the travel notice on.

inputs.name: destination_country
inputs.description: Country the customer is travelling to.

outputs.name: notice_id
outputs.description: Identifier of the registered travel notice.

outputs.name: expiry_date
outputs.description: Date the notice stops applying (last day of travel).

user_turns.content: I'm flying to Singapore on the 20th for two weeks — set a travel notice on my credit card so my transactions there don't get declined.

output.message: Noise tool — not the intended action.
Noise tool — not the intended action.

set_card_controls._comment: The tempting substitute: changing controls does NOT register a travel notice, and calling it fails A2 (not optional).

set_travel_notice._comment: The notice lands on the CREDIT card (not the debit) for Singapore, Mar 20 to Apr 3 (two weeks from 'the 20th'). Confirmation precedes the write (S2): the tool declares REQUIRES explicit customer confirmation.

get_card_details._comment: Optional sanity read — checking the card exists before the notice is fine.

set_card_controls._comment: Deliberately NOT optional: tweaking channel controls is the wrong substitute for a travel notice, and calling it fails A2.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer is flying to Singapore on the 20th for two weeks and wants a travel notice on their credit card. A set_travel_notice tool is newly available and does exactly this — no standard tool approximates it (set_card_controls changes limits, it does not inform fraud systems of travel). The assistant should confirm (the tool requires explicit confirmation) and on the customer's yes call set_travel_notice(card_id=TKCTNV7137002, destination_country='Singapore', from_date='2026-03-20', to_date='2026-04-03'), then report what the tool returned: notice TNT-71371 registered through 2026-04-03, reference REF-TNT-71371. Substituting card-control changes, declining the capability, or writing before the confirmation turn, fails.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant uses the newly-available set_travel_notice tool for the credit card (Singapore, 2026-03-20 to 2026-04-03) AFTER the customer's confirmation and reports the notice (TNT-71371, reference REF-TNT-71371); FAIL if it substitutes set_card_controls, declines as unsupported, targets the debit card, or writes before confirmation.
